# eda-designs

A **framework-agnostic design-token foundation**. The whole system is built on
one idea: **design tokens are the single source of truth**. Everything visual —
colors, typography, spacing, radii — is declared once, as plain JSON, with no
knowledge of React, Vue, Tailwind, or any other framework. A build step
([Style Dictionary](https://styledictionary.com/)) transforms that JSON into
consumable artifacts (today: CSS custom properties; later: whatever a framework
adapter needs).

If a value describes how the product *looks*, it lives in a token. If a value
describes how a *framework* works, it lives in an adapter — never in the tokens.

---

## Why tokens are the source of truth

A design token is a named, platform-neutral design decision — e.g.
"`color.semantic.primary` is this blue", "`space.4` is `1rem`". Because tokens
are just data:

- **One definition, many outputs.** The same `color.json` can generate CSS
  variables, a JS/TS theme object, native platform resources, Figma styles —
  without re-deciding the values.
- **Framework independence.** Tokens contain zero framework assumptions. A
  React adapter (STEP 2) and any future adapter all read from the *same* tokens,
  so the design stays consistent across consumers.
- **Themeable by construction.** Re-theming is "swap the token values, re-run
  the build" — not "hunt through component code".

---

## Repo layout

```
eda-designs/
├── package.json          # declares style-dictionary (devDep) + the "build" script
├── README.md             # this file
├── tokens/               # THE SOURCE OF TRUTH (authored by hand)
│   └── themes/           # one subfolder per named design direction
│       └── default/      # the one shipped direction: color/typography/spacing/radii JSON
├── build/                # Style Dictionary build config (wired in STEP/action a3)
├── dist/                 # GENERATED output — do not edit by hand
│   └── themes/
│       └── <direction>/  # variables.css emitted per direction
├── adapters/             # placeholder → React adapter (STEP 2)
└── docs/                 # placeholder → guidelines + add-a-direction guide (STEP 4)
```

### Where each kind of token lives

All token values live under `tokens/themes/<direction>/`, split by category into
four files:

| Category       | File              | Holds                                                       |
| -------------- | ----------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| **Colors**     | `color.json`      | primitive palette + semantic roles (background, surface, text, primary, border, …) |
| **Typography** | `typography.json` | font families, a modular size scale, weights, line-heights  |
| **Spacing**    | `spacing.json`    | the spacing scale                                           |
| **Radii**      | `radii.json`      | the corner-radius scale                                     |

(These files are authored in the next action — this action only establishes the
skeleton and the build wiring's home.)

---

## Named design directions (themes)

A **design direction** is a complete, self-contained set of token values living
in its own folder under `tokens/themes/`. Each direction supplies *its own*
values for all four categories; the category structure (file names, token
schema, naming convention) is identical across directions so they're
interchangeable.

```
tokens/themes/
├── default/      # the one direction shipped today
│   ├── color.json
│   ├── typography.json
│   ├── spacing.json
│   └── radii.json
└── <next>/       # a future direction: same files, different values
```

The build is **parametrized over the set of direction folders** — it iterates
whatever exists under `tokens/themes/` and emits one CSS file per direction into
`dist/themes/<direction>/variables.css`. So:

**Adding a new direction = copy `tokens/themes/default/`, rename the folder,
substitute values, re-run the build.** No build-config edits required.

---

## Build

```bash
npm install      # installs style-dictionary into node_modules
npm run build    # generates dist/themes/<direction>/variables.css for every direction
```

`npm run build` runs `node build/style-dictionary.config.js`. That script
**discovers every direction folder under `tokens/themes/`** at build time and
runs Style Dictionary once per direction — each build sees *only* that
direction's token files, so directions never leak values into one another. The
output is one `:root { … }` CSS-custom-property bundle per direction:

```
dist/themes/
└── default/
    └── variables.css   # --color-*, --font-*, --space-*, --radius-*
```

Today this produces `dist/themes/default/variables.css` (~3.7 KB) with real
custom properties for all four token categories — colors (primitive + semantic
roles, references resolved to concrete values), typography, spacing, and radii.

### Adding a new direction (high level)

Because the build iterates the direction folders, adding a direction needs **no
build-config changes**:

1. Copy `tokens/themes/default/` to `tokens/themes/<new-direction>/`.
2. Keep the same file names and token paths; substitute the *values*.
3. Run `npm run build` — a new `dist/themes/<new-direction>/variables.css`
   appears automatically.

> The full, opinionated add-a-direction guide (naming, review checklist, etc.)
> lands in `docs/` in STEP 4. The three steps above are the mechanical essence.

---

## Where later steps plug in

| Step       | Adds                                                                                |
| ---------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **tokens** | `tokens/themes/default/*.json` (the four categories) + `tokens/README.md` schema doc |
| **build**  | `build/style-dictionary.config.js`, parametrized over directions → `dist/…/variables.css` |
| **STEP 2** | `adapters/` — a React adapter that consumes the tokens / generated CSS variables     |
| **STEP 4** | `docs/` — usage guidelines + the full add-a-direction guide                          |

---

## Conventions

- **Never edit `dist/` by hand** — it is generated; your changes will be
  overwritten on the next build.
- **Keep tokens framework-agnostic** — no React/CSS-framework values, no
  hardcoded component styles. If it's framework-specific, it belongs in an
  adapter.
- **One token format throughout** — the token files use a single consistent
  Style-Dictionary-compatible format (chosen when the tokens are authored), and
  the build config matches it.
